pages.title: Shop
pages.content:
Shop

Browse our complete catalogue of art supplies, from mill-ordered cotton sheets to studio hand tools. Everything on our shelves is chosen for working illustrators and design students.

Shop by Range

We organize our shelves into four essential ranges: paper, pigment and paint, brushes, and studio tools. Rather than stocking hundreds of overlapping brands, we keep our selection focused and deep. You will find cotton watercolour papers sourced directly from specialist mills, unadulterated dry earth pigments, single pigment watercolour tubes, handmade synthetic sable brushes in balanced sizes, and durable studio knives. Select any range to explore full specifications, sheet dimensions, and technical notes for your studio practice.

Catalogue and Student Discount

Our core catalogue features eight dependable staples kept in steady supply. These include individual cotton watercolour sheets at €7.40, twenty-sheet cotton paper blocks at €38.00, ten-metre sketch paper rolls at €46.00, fifteen-millilitre watercolour tubes at €9.80, and fifty-gram jars of pure earth pigment at €12.50. For brushwork, we supply single round brushes at €21.00 and boxed five-brush cotton rolls at €84.00, alongside our studio palette knife and brass sharpener set at €18.50. All prices include VAT. Students receive a ten percent discount across our entire catalogue with a valid student card, both at our shop counter and online.

How to Order and Filter Items?

You can sort our catalogue by department, format, or price to find the exact supplies your project requires. Items ordered online are packed by hand on Calder Row and dispatched across the European Union for a flat rate of €6.50, with free shipping on all orders over €80. If you prefer to collect your materials in person, free counter collection is available during our regular opening hours from Tuesday through Saturday. Orders for standard items are prepared within one working day of confirmation.

pages.title: Paper
pages.content:
Paper

We stock pure cotton sheets, paper blocks, and rolls chosen specifically for water-based media and printmaking. Every paper on our shelves is acid-free and made for durable studio work.

Cotton Fibre versus Wood Pulp

Cotton rag fibres are significantly longer and more resilient than wood pulp fibres, allowing a sheet to absorb heavy washes without buckling or breaking down under repeated abrasion. Unlike wood pulp, which requires chemical processing to remove lignin and degrades over time, pure cotton is naturally acid-free and maintains its archival brightness for decades. When you work wet-into-wet on cotton paper, pigments sink into the fibres evenly rather than pooling on the surface. This structural difference provides illustrators and printmakers with precise wash control and reliable surface stability.

Paper Specifications and Formats

We stock three standard paper formats on our shop floor. The cotton watercolour sheet is 300 gsm, measures 56 by 76 cm, comes in hot or cold press, and costs €7.40 per sheet. The cotton paper block is 300 gsm, measures 24 by 32 cm with twenty sheets glued on four sides, and costs €38.00. For large preparatory drawings, our natural white sketch paper roll is 120 gsm, measures 1.5 by 10 metres, and costs €46.00. All prices include VAT.

Understanding Hot, Cold, and Rough Surfaces

Choosing a paper surface determines how pigment settles across your composition. Hot-press paper is passed through heated metal cylinders to create a smooth, dense surface that favours delicate pen linework, fine botanical studies, and sharp botanical washes. Cold-press paper is pressed between felt blankets without heat, leaving a medium tooth that balances wash capacity with line control for general illustration. Rough paper dries without heavy pressing, preserving deep valleys where granulation and dry-brush marks break naturally across the textured tooth of the sheet.

Friday Paper Cutting and Mill Orders

Every Friday at Enogu Supply, we cut full paper sheets down to your exact custom working dimensions while you wait at the counter. Jonah Reyes handles our studio guillotine, trimming sheets square with clean, straight edges for bookbinding or portfolio portfolios. If your studio requires large volumes, specific historical watermarks, or unstocked sheet sizes, we place mill orders directly with three partner mills every Thursday at 17:00, with sheets arriving within approximately three weeks.

pages.title: Pigment & Paint
pages.content:
Pigment & Paint

We supply pure dry pigments and single-pigment artists' watercolours designed for clean mixing and permanent lightfastness. All of our colours are formulated without unnecessary fillers or artificial brighteners.

Watercolour Tubes and Pure Dry Pigments

Working from pure dry pigment gives artists complete mastery over vehicle, binder density, and final surface sheen, whether you grind pigment into gum arabic, egg tempera, or walnut oil. Our fifty-gram jars of pure earth pigments contain raw minerals—ochres, umbers, siennas, and terre verte—priced at €12.50 per jar. For immediate studio work, our fifteen-millilitre artists' watercolour tubes provide concentrated series 1 colours at €9.80 per tube. Each tube is milled with pure gum arabic and honey, offering immediate re-wetting and radiant colour payoff.

Lightfastness and Reading Swatch Cards

Every colour we shelf undergoes testing for lightfastness and transparency. Swatch cards displayed along our counter feature two distinct bands: an opaque mass tone drawn across a black indicator line and a dilute wash feathered out on 300 gsm cotton paper. The indicator line demonstrates whether a pigment is transparent, semi-opaque, or completely covering, while the wash reveals tonal undertones and granulation characteristics. We only stock single-pigment formulations with documented archival ratings, ensuring your original paintings remain unchanged when exposed to natural gallery lighting.

Rafael Duarte's Six-Colour Earth Palette

Botanical painter Rafael Duarte visited Calder Row looking to strip away synthetic hues and construct a permanent six-colour earth palette entirely from our fifty-gram pure pigment jars. Working together at the counter with Amara Nwosu, Rafael tested warm and cool mineral undertones, comparing raw and burnt siennas with Italian terre verte and deep raw umbers. Rafael mulled each pigment by hand in his studio with gum arabic, water, and clover honey, creating a tailored set of watercolour pans. This cohesive, mineral-based palette allowed him to depict subtle bark textures, decaying foliage, and delicate root systems with organic harmony, relying entirely on natural mineral sediment rather than synthetic dyes for tonal depth.

pages.title: Brushes
pages.content:
Brushes

Our brush collection is built around balanced synthetic sable rounds and versatile flats designed to hold crisp points and generous wash reservoirs. We encourage every customer to wet and test our brushes before purchasing.

Testing Brushes at the Counter

You cannot evaluate the spring, belly capacity, or point of a brush while its filaments remain stiffened with factory gum. At our shop counter on Calder Row, Amara Nwosu keeps clean water pots and heavy cotton test strips ready for anyone considering a brush. We invite you to dip the hair into water, feel how the tuft snaps back after a loaded sweep, and check how fine the tip remains under light pressure. Experiencing the balance in your hand ensures you leave with a tool suited to your specific hand pressure and painting speed.

Sizes from Two to Twelve and Specifications

We stock synthetic sable rounds in sizes spanning two through twelve. Size 2 and size 4 provide tight control for fine contour linework and tiny botanical details. Size 6 and size 8 serve as core workhorses, holding sufficient pigment for steady rendering while retaining a needle-sharp point. Size 12 carries an expansive water belly capable of laying wide background washes. An individual short-handle size 8 round brush costs €21.00, while our protective cotton brush roll containing five rounds—sizes 2, 4, 6, 8, and 12—is €84.00 including VAT.

How Should You Care for Synthetic Sable Brushes?

Proper cleaning extends the lifespan of synthetic sable filaments for years of continuous studio painting. Always rinse your brushes thoroughly in cool or lukewarm water immediately after painting, taking care never to let paint dry inside the ferrule. Reshape the damp tuft gently with your fingertips and lay the brush flat on a clean towel or suspend it bristles-down to dry. Never leave brushes resting on their hair in a water jar, as this bends the filaments permanently and loosens the wooden handle's protective lacquer.

pages.title: Studio Tools
pages.content:
Studio Tools

We stock the tactile, durable implements that live permanently on studio desks, from solid brass sharpeners to flexible spring-steel knives. Each tool is chosen for mechanical reliability and steady handling.

Essential Hand Tools for the Studio Table

A dependable studio space relies on simple, durable hand tools that perform without distraction. Our curated tool selection centres on balanced steel palette knives, heavy brass pencil sharpeners, basswood drawing boards, and residue-free drafting tape. Our primary palette knife and brass sharpener set costs €18.50 including VAT, featuring two flexible spring-steel knives paired with a solid milled brass sharpener. The cranked knife blades keep knuckles clear of mixing slabs, while the sharpener's hardened steel blade produces needle-fine points on graphite and charcoal pencils without shattering fragile leads.

Additional Studio Supplies on Our Shelves

Alongside our boxed sets, our shelves hold workshop sundries essential for finishing and mounting artwork. We carry sturdy multi-ply wooden drawing boards that resist water absorption, acid-free low-tack drafting tape that lifts from delicate watercolour paper without tearing fibres, hand-carved bone folders for folding paper folios, heavy stainless steel straightedges, and replacement utility blades. Each tool is selected for plain utility and longevity, avoiding plastic parts that crack under everyday studio pressure.

Jonah's Custom Paper Cutting Service

Trimming heavy cotton paper down to custom dimensions can easily ruin expensive full sheets if attempted with blunt blades or unstable straightedges. At Enogu Supply, Jonah Reyes manages our studio cutting bench, preparing boards, sharpening equipment, and trimming paper to your exact millimeter specifications. Every Friday, Jonah cuts full mill sheets down to size while you wait in the shop, producing square edges and clean margins for print editions, custom sketchbooks, or framing mounts.

pages.title: Mill Orders
pages.content:
Mill Orders

We order full paper sheets directly from three historic European paper mills every Thursday at 17:00. This service allows illustrators, printmakers, and institutions to order specialized surfaces in production quantities.

How a Mill Order Runs

Ordering paper directly from our partner mills is straightforward and transparent. First, ask at our counter or email hello@enogu-supply.example with your required sheet size, grammage, and surface texture. Second, we confirm the mill's price and lead time within two working days, requiring a thirty percent deposit upon your confirmation. Third, our consolidated mill orders leave for the mills every Thursday at 17:00 sharp. Fourth, about three weeks later, your sheets arrive at Calder Row; you can collect them in person for free or we post them flat between sturdy boards.

Our Three Partner Mills

We collaborate exclusively with three specialist mills. Aubel Mill specializes in slow-formed 300 gsm and 640 gsm cotton sheets with pronounced, deckled margins and deep sizing suited to heavy aqueous washes. Hartsend Mill produces velvety, pristine hot-press surfaces renowned for crisp botanical rendering, etching editions, and fine ink drawing. Vossberg Mill operates traditional cylinder moulds capable of producing heritage rough and custom textured sheets with irregular, natural tooth. We require a minimum order of ten sheets per paper type to send a custom mill order to any of these makers.

Wrenfield College Degree Show Order

For their final degree show, the graduating illustration cohort at Wrenfield College of Art & Design needed a consistent, high-grade paper stock capable of handling gouache, ink, and lithography across diverse individual projects. Working alongside paper buyer Hanna Weiss, the faculty coordinated a unified 320-sheet mill order of 300 gsm hot-press cotton paper from Hartsend Mill. We submitted the consolidated order ahead of our Thursday 17:00 mill cut-off, confirmed lead times within forty-eight hours, and received the entire shipment three weeks later. When the crates arrived at Calder Row, Tomás Ferreira and Jonah Reyes trimmed specific batches to custom folios before safe studio delivery.

Oona Lind's Custom Paper Search

Picture-book illustrator Oona Lind faced a critical delay on a major publication when the distinctive rough, heavyweight paper she had used for years abruptly ceased production. Desperate to maintain textural consistency across her remaining painted spreads, Oona brought old preliminary swatches to Calder Row. Hanna Weiss examined the fibre structure and contacted Vossberg Mill to locate an archival mould-made paper with equivalent tooth and water absorption. Vossberg Mill matched the formulation, and we placed an order for forty custom sheets. The shipment arrived three weeks later, allowing Oona to complete her book illustrations without any visible break in texture or wash behaviour.

Request a Mill Order

To begin a mill order, speak with Leo Marchetti at our counter or submit your specifications directly. Please include your desired paper mill, sheet dimensions, grammage, surface texture, and sheet quantity, bearing in mind our ten-sheet minimum. We will confirm the mill's exact quote and delivery schedule within two working days. Once your thirty percent deposit is received, your order joins our Thursday 17:00 dispatch. You can collect finished sheets free of charge at Calder Row 9 or have them shipped flat between protective boards.

pages.title: Price List
pages.content:
Price List

Here is the complete pricing schedule for all core catalogue items kept on our shelves at Calder Row 9. All listed prices include VAT and reflect our transparent retail rates.

Complete Catalogue Price Schedule

Our core catalogue consists of eight transparently priced staples. In our paper range, the cotton watercolour sheet (300 gsm, 56 × 76 cm, hot or cold press) is €7.40 per sheet, the cotton paper block (300 gsm, 24 × 32 cm, 20 sheets) is €38.00, and the sketch paper roll (120 gsm, 1.5 × 10 m) is €46.00. For paints, our artists' watercolour tube (15 ml, series 1 colours) is €9.80, and our pure pigment jar (50 g, earth colours) is €12.50. In brushes and tools, the size 8 round brush is €21.00, the brush roll of five rounds is €84.00, and the palette knife and brass sharpener set is €18.50. Prices include VAT. Mill-order paper is quoted per sheet; we confirm within two working days.

Shipping Rates and Flat Packing

We post orders across the European Union at a flat rate of €6.50, with free shipping applied automatically to all orders over €80. Because rolled watercolour paper develops an unwanted curl that complicates studio work, every single sheet of paper is packed flat between two rigid, multi-ply grey corrugated boards with reinforced corner guards. Packages are taped securely and dispatched by Leo Marchetti on Mondays. In-person collection at our shop on Calder Row is always free of charge during regular opening hours.

Student Discounts and Mill Order Terms

We offer a ten percent student discount on all retail supplies to support emerging illustrators and designers. Present a valid student card at our shop counter to receive your in-store discount and an online code for web purchases. For custom mill orders of ten sheets or more from Aubel Mill, Hartsend Mill, or Vossberg Mill, we quote prices directly per sheet based on mill production runs. Mill order quotes are confirmed within two working days and require a thirty percent deposit upon confirmation.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content:
Visit

Enogu Supply is located at Calder Row 9 in Wrenfield, open five days a week for paper consultations, brush testing, and studio supplies. We welcome working artists, students, and visitors to our counters.

The Weekly Shop Schedule

Our shop week follows a deliberate working rhythm across five open days. On Monday, we are closed while Leo packs and posts the week's orders. On Tuesday, we open from 10:00 to 18:30 as fresh mill crates arrive and are unpacked into our plan chests. On Wednesday, we restock shelves and offer dedicated brush testing at the counter from 10:00 to 18:30. Thursday features late opening until 20:00, with our mill-order cut-off at 17:00 and Sun-hee's demo evening from 18:30 to 20:00. On Friday (10:00–18:30), paper is cut to size while you wait. Saturday (10:00–18:30) is our busiest day, featuring Mira's student desk. We are closed on Sunday.

Thursday Demo Evenings with Sun-hee Park

Every Thursday evening between 18:30 and 20:00, illustrator Sun-hee Park hosts an informal, practical demonstration at our central oak table. Sun-hee covers essential studio techniques, from preparing raw pigments with natural binders to managing wet-on-dry brush drag on textured mould-made paper. Attendance is free and open to everyone without prior booking. Visitors can observe professional working methods up close, ask detailed technical questions about media interactions, and handle materials directly in an unhurried, collaborative studio atmosphere while the shop remains open late.

Location, Transit, and Accessibility

Enogu Supply is situated at Calder Row 9 in central Wrenfield. The shop is easily accessible by public transit, located just a three-minute walk from the Calder Row tram stop. Ample municipal bicycle racks are installed directly in front of our entrance for cyclists. Our shop floor features a wide, step-free entrance from street level, allowing smooth accessibility for wheelchairs, prams, and heavy portfolio cases. Wide aisles provide unobstructed navigation between our plan chests, pigment displays, and cutting counters.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Founded in 2011, Enogu Supply is an independent art-supply shop committed to providing uncompromised paper, pigments, and tools for illustrators and design students. We keep our range intentionally narrow, deep, and dependable.

Our Origin on Calder Row

Hanna Weiss opened Enogu Supply in 2011 on Calder Row with a single shallow plan chest and a small shipment of cotton papers that were impossible to find locally. Having worked closely with printmakers and illustrators, Hanna recognized that artists were frustrated by mass-market shops full of decorative novelties and degraded student-grade materials. She set out to build an unhurried shop dedicated to archival essentials: pure cotton papers, lightfast single-pigment watercolours, and handmade brushes that hold a true point under pressure.

Our Approach to Stock and Principles

Today, our shelves hold 1,240 carefully selected items across four distinct categories. We order directly from 3 independent paper mills and stay open 5 days a week, keeping our focus narrow so we can stock each range in genuine depth. We do not stock synthetic novelties, unrated paints, or multi-packs of low-grade brushes. Every tool, pigment jar, and paper block on Calder Row is evaluated for structural durability, tactile balance, and material permanence before earning a permanent drawer on our shop floor.

The Seven People at Enogu Supply

Our shop is run by a dedicated seven-person team: Hanna Weiss — founder and paper buyer, who established Enogu Supply in 2011 and maintains our direct relationships with European paper mills. Tomás Ferreira — shop clerk, who oversees our wide plan chests and assists customers with individual paper selections. Amara Nwosu — brush and pigment counter clerk, who guides artists through pigment lightfastness and counter brush testing. Leo Marchetti — logistics coordinator, who manages mill order consignments and packs our flat mailings every Monday. Sun-hee Park — resident illustrator, who leads our Thursday evening demonstrations on pigment mixing and brush handling. Mira Kowal — Saturday clerk, who runs our dedicated student advice desk and issues educational discount codes. Jonah Reyes — studio tool specialist, who maintains our cutting bench and provides custom Friday paper trimming.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

Get in touch with our shop team on Calder Row for paper inquiries, mill order details, or counter collections. We read and answer every message within two working days.

Shop Location and Direct Contact Details

You can reach Enogu Supply by phone at +00 31 555 0148 or by sending an email to hello@enogu-supply.example. Our shop is located at Calder Row 9 in Wrenfield. We are open five days a week: Tuesday through Saturday from 10:00 to 18:30, with late hours on Thursday until 20:00 for our weekly demonstration evening. We are closed on Sunday and Monday, when Leo packs and dispatches weekly mail orders. Our staff reviews incoming correspondence daily and responds within two working days.

Enquiries and Mill Order Guidance

Whether you have questions regarding specific pigment toxicity, need advice on choosing between cold-press and rough paper surfaces, or wish to initiate a custom paper order from Aubel Mill, Hartsend Mill, or Vossberg Mill, we are pleased to assist. When inquiring about mill orders, please specify your intended sheet dimensions, grammage, and quantity so that we can calculate an accurate quote and delivery timeline within our standard two-day review window.

How to Send Us a Message?

You can send an enquiry directly using our contact form. Fill in your name, email address, project subject, and message details. If form processing is unavailable, activating the submission button launches a mailto draft directly to hello@enogu-supply.example through your default email client. We treat all studio enquiries with care and will respond directly to your inbox within two working days to assist with your art supply requirements.

posts.title: How We Pack a Mill Order
posts.excerpt: Inside our Monday studio routine on Calder Row, where Leo Marchetti prepares and packs full sheets of mill-ordered cotton paper between rigid boards for safe travel.
posts.content:
Every Monday morning, while the front entrance of Enogu Supply at Calder Row 9 remains locked to the street, our workshop behind the counter is in full motion. Monday is our dedicated packing and posting day. Outside, Wrenfield is quiet, but inside, Leo Marchetti clears our long ash-wood packing table, sweeps away stray paper off-cuts, and prepares the dispatch bench. Over the preceding days, wooden crates shipped from our partner mills—Aubel Mill, Hartsend Mill, and Vossberg Mill—have been unpacked and catalogued into our shallow plan chests. Now, the custom mill orders and online paper purchases must be readied for their journeys to studios across the European Union.

Packing fine paper is an exacting discipline. When artists invest in 300 gsm cotton watercolour sheets measuring 56 by 76 cm, they expect pristine, undisturbed surfaces. Many mass-market art retailers cut corners by rolling heavy cotton paper into cardboard mailing tubes. We refuse to roll our paper. Heavy mould-made cotton fibres have a delicate internal structure and a gelatin surface sizing that can craze or stretch when forced into a tight curve. Worse, uncurling a stiff 300 gsm sheet before painting creates surface tension, making flat washes difficult to control and increasing the risk of dog-eared corners.

Instead, Leo packs every sheet completely flat. The process begins with two oversized sheets of rigid, multi-ply grey corrugated backing board, cut slightly larger than the 56 by 76 cm cotton sheets to leave a protective border on all four sides. Leo lays the first backing board flat on the bench and covers it with clean, acid-free interleaving tissue. Working with clean hands, he draws the cotton sheets from the drawers, verifying the surface texture—whether velvety hot-press, toothy cold-press, or textured rough from Vossberg Mill—and gently aligns them. A second layer of interleaving tissue covers the top sheet to shield the delicate deckled edges from abrasion.

Next comes the structural reinforcement. Leo places the second rigid board on top, sandwiching the paper securely inside. To protect the corners from crushing during transport, he slips custom heavy-duty corner guards over all four corners of the sandwich. These guards disperse any impact if a parcel is dropped on edge. Leo then bands the package using strong linen twine, pulling it taut enough to prevent internal shifting without crimping the outer boards. A final moisture barrier is wrapped around the exterior before the delivery label is applied.

Every parcel packed on Monday leaves with our standard flat-rate European Union shipping of €6.50, or completely free of charge for orders over €80. By the time our shop reopens on Tuesday morning at 10:00 for the arrival of new crates, the week's postal orders are on their way. Taking this extra time to pack paper flat between boards ensures that when an illustrator unboxes a mill order in their studio, the sheets are as pristine, flat, and ready for water as they were the moment they left the mill mould.
